'''Jill Catherine Pipher''' (born December 14, 1955, in [[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania]]) is an American mathematician. She served as president of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS, 2019–2020)<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/officers/officers|title=Officers of the American Mathematical Society|access-date=2019-03-13|language=en}}</ref> and president of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM, 2011–2013). She was the first director of the [[Institute for Computational and Experimental Research in Mathematics]] (ICERM, 2011–2016), an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]]-funded mathematics institute based in [[Providence, Rhode Island]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/presidents/65-pipher|title=AMS Presidents:Jill Pipher|access-date=2024-02-15|language=en}}</ref>

==Contributions==
Pipher's research areas include [[harmonic analysis]], [[Fourier analysis]], [[partial differential equations]], and [[cryptography]].  She has published more than 60 research articles and has coauthored with Jeffrey Hoffstein and Joseph Silverman a textbook titled ''An Introduction to Mathematical Cryptography''.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/us/book/9781441926746|title=An Introduction to Mathematical Cryptography {{!}} Jeffrey Hoffstein {{!}} Springer|language=en}}</ref> 

==Education and career==
Pipher is currently the [[Elisha Andrews|Elisha Benjamin Andrews]] Professor of Mathematics at [[Brown University]].  She received a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1979 and a PhD from UCLA in 1985 under the direction of [[John B. Garnett]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=25304}}</ref> She taught at the [[University of Chicago]] (1985–1990) before taking a position at Brown in 1990, where she served as chair of the Mathematics Department from 2005 to 2008.

In 1996, Pipher, along with [[Jeffrey Hoffstein]], [[Daniel Lieman]] and [[Joseph H. Silverman|Joseph Silverman]], founded NTRU Cryptosystems, Inc., now part of Security Innovation, Inc. to market their cryptographic algorithms, [[NTRUEncrypt]] and [[NTRUSign]]. 

==Recognition==
In 2012 she became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-05-05.</ref>  In 2017, she was selected as a fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in the inaugural class.<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 Inaugural Class of AWM Fellows|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/|website=awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2018-awm-fellows|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref> In 2019 she was named a [[SIAM Fellow]] "for her profound contributions in analysis and partial differential equations, groundbreaking work in public key cryptography, and outstanding scientific leadership".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/Prizes-Recognition/Fellows-Program/All-SIAM-Fellows/Class-of-2019|title=SIAM Fellows Class of 2019|access-date=2019-09-01}}</ref> She was named to the 2021 class of Fellows of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/page/2021-fellows|title=2021 Fellows|publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science|access-date=2022-01-28}}</ref>

In 2014 Pipher was a [[Mathematical Association of America]] Invited Lecturer at the [[Joint Mathematics Meetings]], speaking on ''The Mathematics of Lattice-based Cryptography''<ref name="JMM Featured Speakers">{{cite web|last=Pipher|first=Jill|title=2014 Joint Mathematics Meetings Highlighted Speakers|url=https://jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm2014/2160_speakers|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=23 May 2014}}</ref> The [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] named her as their [[Noether Lecture]]r for 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/noether-lectures/noether-lectures-2018/|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|title=2018 Lecturer: Jill Pipher|work=Emmy Noether Lectures|access-date=2024-03-03}}</ref>

In 2019–2020, she served as the 65th president of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.brown.edu/articles/2017/12/pipher|title=Pipher to become president of the American Mathematical Society|access-date=2017-12-09|language=en}}</ref> She was the third woman to be elected to this position, following [[Julia Robinson]] (1983–1984) and [[Cathleen Synge Morawetz]] (1995–1996).
